title: Arizona AASA (7th Grade)
description: Arizona Academic Standards Assessment prep for 7th grade - Math and ELA

questions.question: A bag has 4 red marbles for every 6 blue marbles. If there are 12 red marbles, how many blue marbles are there?
questions.explanation: The ratio is 4 red to 6 blue. 12 red marbles is 4 times 3, so multiply the blue side by 3 as well: 6 x 3 = 18 blue marbles.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: what you do to one side of a ratio, do to the other - like stomping both feet at the same time!

questions.question: What is 20% of 60?
questions.explanation: 20% of 60 = 0.20 x 60 = 12. You can also think: 10% of 60 is 6, so 20% is twice that: 6 x 2 = 12.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 20% is 2 out of every 10 dino eggs - a tiny roar of a slice!

questions.question: A truck drives 120 miles in 2 hours at a constant speed. What is its unit rate in miles per hour?
questions.explanation: Unit rate means divide: 120 miles / 2 hours = 60 miles per hour.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: unit rate means one unit at a time - one stomp, one hour, one answer!

questions.question: A recipe calls for 2 cups of flour for every 3 cups of sugar. How many cups of sugar are needed for 8 cups of flour?
questions.explanation: The recipe ratio is 2 flour to 3 sugar. 8 cups of flour is 4 times 2, so multiply the sugar by 4 too: 3 x 4 = 12 cups of sugar.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: scale recipes like a dino buffet - multiply every ingredient by the same number or the cake will stomp flat!

questions.question: A store sells 5 pens for $8. How much would 12 pens cost at the same rate?
questions.explanation: First find the unit rate: $8 / 5 pens = $1.60 per pen. Then multiply: $1.60 x 12 pens = $19.20.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: find the price of one little egg before you buy the whole nest - unit rate first!

questions.question: 45 students signed up for the field trip. If there are 150 students total, what percent signed up?
questions.explanation: Percent = part / whole x 100. 45 / 150 = 0.3, and 0.3 x 100 = 30%.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: percent means out of a hundred - shrink the whole thing down to a cozy little dino den of 100!

questions.question: On a map, 1 inch represents 25 miles. Two towns are 4.5 inches apart on the map. How many miles apart are they really?
questions.explanation: Set up the proportion: 1 inch / 25 miles = 4.5 inches / x miles. Cross multiply: x = 4.5 x 25 = 112.5 miles.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cross multiply like dino legs crossing on a hike - left foot times right foot's partner!

questions.question: In a band the ratio of trumpets to drums is 3 to 4. There are 28 more drums than trumpets. How many drums are there?
questions.explanation: Trumpets to drums = 3 to 4, so drums have 1 part more. That 1 part = 28 students. Drums = 4 parts: 4 x 28 = 112 drums.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: when the gap tells the secret, the gap is the key - one ratio part hides the whole answer!

questions.question: A jacket is on sale for $84 after a 30% discount. What was the original price of the jacket?
questions.explanation: After a 30% discount the jacket is 70% of its original price. So 0.70 x original = $84. Divide: $84 / 0.70 = $120.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a discount leaves a leftover percent - find what survived, not what the dino ate!

questions.question: A car uses 9 gallons of gas to drive 216 miles. At the same rate, how many miles can it drive on 15 gallons?
questions.explanation: First find miles per gallon: 216 / 9 = 24 miles per gallon. Then multiply: 24 x 15 = 360 miles.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: feed the car its fuel and count how far each gallon stomps - unit rate before the big trip!

questions.question: A car travels 240 miles in 4 hours. What is its speed in miles per hour?
questions.explanation: 240 miles / 4 hours = 60 miles per hour. Divide total miles by total hours to get the unit rate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: unit rate is just one dino-step at a time - divide to find one!

questions.question: A pack of 6 granola bars costs $4.80. What is the price per bar?
questions.explanation: 4.80 / 6 = 0.80. Divide the total price by the number of bars to get the unit price.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy snacks one bar at a time and always pays the single-bar price!

questions.question: Solve the proportion: x / 9 = 14 / 6. What is x?
questions.explanation: Cross-multiply: 6 times x = 9 times 14, so 6x = 126. Then x = 126 / 6 = 21.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy crosses the jungle diagonally to solve proportions - cross-multiply!

questions.question: A bike shop sells a $90 helmet for 25% off. What is the sale price?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy always checks the FINAL price after the discount, not just the savings!

questions.question: A restaurant bill is $50.00. Maya leaves a 20% tip. What is the tip amount?
questions.explanation: Tip = 0.20 times 50 = 10. Multiply the bill by the tip rate: 50 times 20/100 = 10.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy tips in tiny claws - 20 percent means twenty cents on every dollar!

questions.question: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for 12 muffins. How many cups of flour are needed for 28 muffins?
questions.explanation: Set up the proportion: 3 / 12 = x / 28. Cross-multiply: 12x = 84, so x = 84 / 12 = 7 cups.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy scales recipes like a proportional pro - keep the ratio and grow!

questions.question: A store adds 8% sales tax to a $75 jacket. What is the total price with tax?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy pays the whole roar - price PLUS tax, not just the tax alone!

questions.question: The price of a skateboard rose from $120 to $150. What is the percent increase?
questions.explanation: Increase = 150 - 120 = 30. Percent increase = 30 / 120 = 0.25 = 25%. Always divide by the ORIGINAL amount.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy compares the change to the STARTING size - divide by the original, roar!

questions.question: A video game costs $45.99 after a 15% discount. Rounded to the nearest cent, what was the original price?
questions.explanation: Sale price = original times (1 - 0.15) = original times 0.85. So original = 45.99 / 0.85 = 54.1058..., which rounds to 54.11.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy works the discount backwards - divide by what is LEFT after the cut!

questions.question: A factory makes 7,200 bottles in 3 shifts. If each shift is 8 hours and bottles are made at a constant rate, how many bottles per hour is that?
questions.explanation: Total hours = 3 shifts times 8 hours = 24 hours. Unit rate = 7,200 bottles / 24 hours = 300 bottles per hour.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy counts every hour first - add up the shifts before you divide!

questions.question: What is -5 + 3?
questions.explanation: -5 + 3 = -2. When adding numbers with different signs, subtract the absolute values (5 - 3 = 2) and keep the sign of the larger one (negative).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: adding a positive to a negative is like the dino climbing back up out of the cold cave - subtract and keep the bigger sign!

questions.question: What is 4 - 9?
questions.explanation: 4 - 9 = -5. Since 9 is larger than 4, you spend past zero into negative land: 9 - 4 = 5, so the answer is -5.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: when the dino digs deeper than ground level, the number goes below zero - past zero means negative!

questions.question: What is -2 + (-7)?
questions.explanation: -2 + (-7) = -9. When both numbers are negative, add the absolute values (2 + 7 = 9) and keep the negative sign.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two negatives together mean the dino is digging deeper and deeper - add them up and stay negative!

questions.question: The temperature was -4 degrees and dropped 7 more degrees. What is the new temperature?
questions.explanation: Start at -4, then drop 7 more: -4 - 7 = -11. Dropping from an already negative temperature moves further below zero, so the answer is -11 degrees.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: when it gets colder than cold, the dino grabs an extra blanket and the number drops below zero - add and stay negative!

questions.question: What is 6 - (-3)?
questions.explanation: 6 - (-3) = 6 + 3 = 9. Subtracting a negative is the same as adding its positive opposite, so 6 + 3 = 9.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: minus a minus means the purple tail grabs the green one and flips it - subtracting a negative turns into adding!

questions.question: A submarine is at -120 feet and rises 45 feet. What is its new depth?
questions.explanation: Rising means adding a positive: -120 + 45 = -75. Since 120 is larger than 45, subtract (120 - 45 = 75) and keep the negative sign, so -75 feet.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the dino submarine floats up out of the deep - subtract and keep the bigger sign!

questions.question: What is -12 - 5?
questions.explanation: -12 - 5 = -17. Subtracting a positive moves further down the number line, so add the absolute values (12 + 5 = 17) and keep the negative sign.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: taking away more from the dino's hole just makes the hole deeper - add the numbers, stay negative!

questions.question: Your bank account has -$25. You deposit $60, then withdraw $40. What is the balance?
questions.explanation: Step 1: deposit $60 into -$25: -25 + 60 = 35. Step 2: withdraw $40: 35 - 40 = -5. The final balance is -$5.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the dino banker adds your deposits but subtracts your snacks - track each step one at a time!

questions.question: What is -8 - (-15)?
questions.explanation: -8 - (-15) = -8 + 15 = 7. Subtracting a negative becomes addition, then combine the different signs: 15 - 8 = 7, and 15 is larger so the answer is positive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the double minus does the dino dance - two left feet turn right, so subtract-a-negative becomes add!

questions.question: The temperature at sunrise was -6 degrees. By noon it rose 14 degrees, then by midnight it fell 21 degrees. What is the midnight temperature?
questions.explanation: Step 1: rise from sunrise to noon: -6 + 14 = 8. Step 2: fall from noon to midnight: 8 - 21 = -13. The midnight temperature is -13 degrees.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the dino rides the temperature seesaw - up at noon, then way down at midnight - work step by step!

questions.question: What is -6 x 4?
questions.explanation: Multiply the numbers: 6 x 4 = 24. A negative times a positive gives a negative, so -6 x 4 = -24.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a grumpy minus times a happy plus gives minus - a grumpy dino result!

questions.question: What is 20 / (-5)?
questions.explanation: Divide the numbers: 20 / 5 = 4. A positive divided by a negative gives a negative, so 20 / (-5) = -4.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plus divided by minus gives minus - even a mighty dino shares the grump!

questions.question: What is (-3) x (-7)?
questions.explanation: Multiply the numbers: 3 x 7 = 21. Two negatives make a positive, so (-3) x (-7) = 21.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: minus times minus gives plus - just like the purple tail meets the green!

questions.question: What is (-72) / 9?
questions.explanation: Divide the numbers: 72 / 9 = 8. A negative divided by a positive gives a negative, so (-72) / 9 = -8.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: negative split by positive stays negative - share the grump, stomp the rest!

questions.question: What is (-5) x 6 x (-2)?
questions.explanation: Multiply left to right. First (-5) x 6 = -30. Then (-30) x (-2) = 60. The two minuses at the end flip it to a positive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: count the minuses! One minus is grumpy, but two minuses flip to plus!

questions.question: What is -4 x (-3) - 20?
questions.explanation: Multiply first: -4 x (-3) = 12, because two negatives make a positive. Then subtract: 12 - 20 = -8.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: minus times minus gives a happy plus, then 12 loses 20 snacks and goes grumpy!

questions.question: What is (-100) / (-4)?
questions.explanation: Divide the numbers: 100 / 4 = 25. A negative divided by a negative gives a positive, so (-100) / (-4) = 25.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two grumpy minuses cancel out - a double stomp makes a happy plus!

questions.question: What is -2 x 3 x (-4) x (-1)?
questions.explanation: Multiply left to right. First -2 x 3 = -6. Then -6 x (-4) = 24. Then 24 x (-1) = -24. Three minus signs is an odd count, so the answer stays negative.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: count the minuses - three grumps is odd, so the answer stays grumpy!

questions.question: What is (-144) / (-12) - (-5) x 2?
questions.explanation: Do division and multiplication before subtraction. (-144) / (-12) = 12 and (-5) x 2 = -10. Then 12 - (-10) = 12 + 10 = 22.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: subtracting a grumpy minus means you ADD the snacks - 12 plus 10 is a dino feast!

questions.question: What is (12 - 4 x 3) x (-2)?
questions.explanation: Work inside the parentheses first. Multiply before subtracting: 4 x 3 = 12. Then 12 - 12 = 0. Finally 0 x (-2) = 0, because anything times zero is zero.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: zero stomps everything flat - multiply by zero and the answer is extinct!

questions.question: Evaluate 3x + 5 when x = 4.
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 4: 3(4) + 5 = 12 + 5 = 17. Watch out: adding 3 + 5 before multiplying gives 32, which is wrong - multiply first.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plug in the number like feeding the dino - substitute first, then solve!

questions.question: Simplify 2a + 5a - 3a.
questions.explanation: 2a + 5a - 3a = (2 + 5 - 3)a = 4a. Like terms are all a's, so just combine their numbers and keep the a.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: like terms stick together like a dino herd - 2a and 5a are family!

questions.question: Which expression represents '5 less than a number x'?
questions.explanation: '5 less than a number x' means start with x and take away 5: x - 5. The order matters - 5 - x means the opposite.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'less than' flips the words - the dino chomps from the front!

questions.question: Evaluate 2y^2 - 3 when y = 5.
questions.explanation: Substitute y = 5: 2(5)^2 - 3 = 2(25) - 3 = 50 - 3 = 47. The exponent comes before multiplying by 2 - squaring 2y instead gives 97.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: exponents stomp first - the dino squares the number before multiplying!

questions.question: Simplify 4x + 3y - 2x + 5.
questions.explanation: Group the like terms: 4x - 2x = 2x, and 3y and 5 have no partners, so the simplified form is 2x + 3y + 5. Never mash x's and y's together.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: x-dinos and y-dinos eat at separate tables - only combine matching letters!

questions.question: Expand 3(2x + 4).
questions.explanation: Distribute the 3 to both terms inside: 3(2x) + 3(4) = 6x + 12. Forgetting the second term gives 6x + 4.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the distributive dino shares with EVERYONE inside the parentheses - no snack skipped!

questions.question: Evaluate 4m - 2n when m = 6 and n = 8.
questions.explanation: Substitute m = 6 and n = 8: 4(6) - 2(8) = 24 - 16 = 8. Keep the minus sign attached to the 2n - adding instead gives 40.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two letters, two feeds - swap in both numbers and mind the minus!

questions.question: Simplify 2(3x - 5) + 4(x + 1).
questions.explanation: First distribute: 2(3x - 5) = 6x - 10 and 4(x + 1) = 4x + 4. Then combine like terms: 6x + 4x = 10x and -10 + 4 = -6, so the answer is 10x - 6.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: distribute BOTH herds, then let the matching dinos march together - signs stay with their owners!

questions.question: Evaluate x^2 + 3(x - 4) when x = 7.
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 7: (7)^2 + 3(7 - 4) = 49 + 3(3) = 49 + 9 = 58. Solving the parentheses first and squaring only the 7 matters - skipping parentheses gives 66.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: parentheses are the dino's mouth - chew what is inside first, then square, then add!

questions.question: Which expression represents 'twice the difference of a number k and 9'?
questions.explanation: 'Twice the difference of a number k and 9' means first find the difference (k - 9), then double the whole thing: 2(k - 9). The parentheses keep 'difference' together - 2k - 9 only doubles the k.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'twice the difference' means the dino doubles the WHOLE herd - trap it in parentheses!

questions.question: Solve for x: x + 5 = 12.
questions.explanation: Subtract 5 from both sides: x = 12 - 5. So x = 7.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: plus is a party crasher - send it back home with a minus!

questions.question: Solve for x: x - 9 = 4.
questions.explanation: Add 9 to both sides: x = 4 + 9. So x = 13.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: undo a minus with a plus, like a dino doing a U-turn!

questions.question: Solve for x: 3x = 24.
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by 3: x = 24 / 3. So x = 8.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the number hugging x gets voted off with division!

questions.question: Solve for x: 2x + 3 = 11.
questions.explanation: Subtract 3 first: 2x = 8. Then divide by 2: x = 4.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: undo the equation backwards like rewinding dino footprints - subtract first, then divide!

questions.question: Solve for x: 6x - 9 = 27.
questions.explanation: Add 9 first: 6x = 36. Then divide by 6: x = 6.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: peel the dino egg from the outside in - add 9 first, then divide by 6!

questions.question: A bag has 5 red marbles and 3 blue marbles. What is the probability of picking a red marble?
questions.explanation: Favorable outcomes = 5 red. Total outcomes = 5 + 3 = 8. So P = 5/8.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: probability is a dino snack count - yummy ones on top, all snacks on the bottom!

questions.question: Find the median of: 1, 2, 3, 10, 11.
questions.explanation: The numbers are already in order: 1, 2, 3, 10, 11. The middle number is 3. So the median is 3.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: median is the dino in the middle of the parade - line them up smallest to biggest first!

questions.question: Find the range of: 12, 18, 7, 15, 10.
questions.explanation: Biggest value = 18. Smallest value = 7. Range = 18 - 7 = 11.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: range is the dino's long jump - from the tiniest toe to the tallest tail tip!

questions.question: T-Rexy flipped a coin 40 times and got heads 24 times. What is the experimental probability of heads?
questions.explanation: Experimental probability = what actually happened / total trials = 24/40. Simplify: 24/40 = 3/5.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: experimental is a real dino field trip - count what REALLY happened, not what you hoped!

questions.question: Five quiz scores have a mean of 12. Four of the scores are 9, 14, 10, and 15. What is the fifth score?
questions.explanation: Mean = total / 5, so total = 12 x 5 = 60. The four known scores add to 9 + 14 + 10 + 15 = 48. Fifth score = 60 - 48 = 12.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: work backwards like a clever raptor - multiply the mean back into the total first!

questions.question: Read: 'First, the seeds are planted in the spring. Next, the sprouts push through the soil. Finally, the tall sunflowers bloom in summer.' What text structure is used?
questions.explanation: The signal words 'First,' 'Next,' and 'Finally' show steps in time order, which is sequence/chronological structure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sequence words march in a line like dinos on a trail - first, next, then, finally!

questions.question: Read: 'The desert is dry and hot during the day, while the forest is damp and cool. Deserts get little rain, whereas forests get rain often. Both places have animals that have adapted to survive.' What text structure is used?
questions.explanation: The signal words 'while,' 'whereas,' and 'Both' show how two places are alike and different, which is compare and contrast structure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: compare and contrast is like two dinos side by side - same and different!

questions.question: Read: 'Because the bridge was damaged in the storm, the town built a new one. As a result, traffic could flow across the river again.' What text structure is used?
questions.explanation: The signal words 'Because' and 'As a result' show a reason and what happened because of it, which is cause and effect structure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cause and effect is like a dino stomping - stomp (cause), then crack (effect)!

questions.question: Read: 'Litter was piling up in the school park. To solve this, students placed recycling bins along every path. Now the park stays clean each week.' What text structure is used?
questions.explanation: The passage first states a problem (litter) and then explains the fix ('To solve this'), which is problem and solution structure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: problem and solution is a dino who sees a blocked trail and smashes a new path!

questions.question: Read: 'The lighthouse stood tall on the rocky cliff. Its bright white tower rose above the waves, and its powerful beam swept across the dark water every few seconds.' What text structure is used?
questions.explanation: The passage lists details about what the lighthouse looks like, using descriptive language rather than order, causes, or comparisons, which is description structure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: description paints a dino portrait with words - colors, shapes, and sizes!

questions.question: Read: 'Since the river flooded the fields, the crops failed. Consequently, the village had to import food for the winter.' What text structure is used?
questions.explanation: The signal words 'Since' and 'Consequently' link a reason to its outcome, not just events in time order, which is cause and effect.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: if one thing makes the other happen, it is cause and effect - not just first, second, third!

questions.question: Read: 'Eagles and hawks are both birds of prey. However, eagles are much larger, and unlike hawks, they build their nests on high cliffs.' What text structure is used?
questions.explanation: The signal words 'both,' 'However,' and 'unlike' highlight similarities and differences between eagles and hawks, which is compare and contrast structure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: both and however are the secret handshake of comparing dinos!

questions.question: Read: 'The museum's new exhibit is arranged by century. It begins with tools from the 1700s, then moves to inventions of the 1800s, and ends with technology of today.' What text structure is used to organize the exhibit?
questions.explanation: Arranging by century with signal words like 'begins,' 'then,' and 'ends' puts items in time order, helping the reader see how technology changed over time, which is sequence/chronological structure.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a timeline is a dino parade - oldest fossils first, newest footprints last!

questions.question: Read: 'The library was losing books each month, so the staff added security tags. Nevertheless, the problem continued, therefore the library installed checkout scanners as a second measure.' What is the MAIN text structure of this passage?
questions.explanation: The passage names a problem (losing books) and gives solutions (security tags, checkout scanners). The words 'so' and 'therefore' show cause and effect inside it, but the main purpose is problem and solution.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sometimes a passage mixes structures - spot the MAIN job the author is doing!

questions.question: Read: 'Solar panels work well in sunny regions. In contrast, wind turbines work best where winds are strong. On the other hand, hydroelectric dams need rivers, yet all three produce clean energy.' Why does compare and contrast help the reader here?
questions.correctAnswer: It puts the three energy sources side by side so the reader can weigh how they differ and what conditions each one needs.
distractors: It lists the steps for building each energy source in the order they were invented.
It explains the problem of dirty air and shows how each source solves it.
It describes each energy source's size, color, and shape in detail.
questions.explanation: The phrases 'In contrast' and 'On the other hand' point out how solar, wind, and hydro power differ. Comparing and contrasting them helps the reader see that each source works best in a different kind of place, so the reader can judge which one fits where.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: comparing three dinos at once still counts - look for the contrast words!

questions.question: Source 1: 'School uniforms help students feel equal and focused on learning.' Source 2: 'School uniforms stop students from showing their personal style.' Which source best supports an argument FOR school uniforms?
questions.explanation: Source 1 gives reasons in favor of uniforms (feeling equal and focused), while Source 2 argues against them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: match the source to the side - a dino cheering FOR the herd joins the FOR team!

questions.question: Source 1: 'Recess gives kids exercise and fresh air every day.' Source 2: 'Recess lets students burn energy so they can focus better in class.' Which source provides a reason for how recess helps LEARNING?
questions.explanation: Source 2 connects recess to learning by saying students can focus better in class. Source 1 only talks about health benefits, not learning.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: check the footprints - does the source actually lead to the claim you need?

questions.question: Source 1: 'Reading for fun helps students learn new words.' Source 2: 'I love reading because it is the best thing ever!' Which source is a FACT that could be used as evidence in an essay?
questions.explanation: Source 1 states a claim that can be checked and tested (reading helps vocabulary), while Source 2 is just a personal opinion about liking reading.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: facts leave footprints you can follow - opinions are just roars in the jungle!

questions.question: Source 1: 'Zoos protect endangered animals and teach visitors about wildlife.' Source 2: 'Some zoo enclosures are too small for large animals to move freely.' Which statement best describes how the two sources are alike?
questions.correctAnswer: Both sources are about zoos but take opposite points of view
distractors: Both sources agree that zoos should be closed
Both sources describe the same zoo
Both sources are written by zookeepers
questions.explanation: Source 1 defends zoos (protection, education) while Source 2 criticizes them (enclosures too small), so they share a topic but differ in point of view.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two dinos, two opinions - same watering hole, different roars!

questions.question: Source 1: 'Video games waste time that kids could spend studying.' Source 2: 'A study found that students who play puzzle games score higher on problem-solving tests.' Which source gives STRONGER evidence about video games and learning?
questions.explanation: Source 2 cites a study with actual test results, which is specific evidence. Source 1 only states an opinion without any supporting data.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a study is a fossil - real proof in the rock! An opinion is just a stomp mark.

questions.question: Source 1: 'The cafeteria should sell pizza every day because pizza is delicious.' Source 2: 'The cafeteria should add more vegetables because the school nurse says students need better nutrition.' Which source is written to persuade readers to make a HEALTHY choice?
questions.explanation: Source 2 argues for vegetables using a health reason backed by the school nurse, while Source 1 only argues for pizza based on taste.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sniff out the author's purpose - which dino is hunting for health points?

questions.question: Source 1: 'Every student should get a tablet because technology is the future of education.' Source 2: 'Our school gave every student a tablet last year, and homework completion rose from 70% to 92%.' Which source provides STRONGER support for the claim that tablets help students learn?
questions.explanation: Source 2 provides real numbers from the school's own experience showing improvement. Source 1 only makes a general claim about the future without any evidence.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: numbers are footprints - you can measure them! Big claims without data are just shadows.

questions.question: Source 1: 'Plastic water bottles are convenient for athletes during games.' Source 2: 'Our town's recycling center reports that plastic bottles make up 40% of local landfill waste.' A writer is arguing that single-use plastic bottles should be banned at sports events. Which source best supports that argument, and why?
questions.correctAnswer: Source 2, because it gives a statistic about plastic bottle waste
distractors: Source 1, because it mentions sports events
Source 2, because it praises recycling centers
questions.explanation: Source 2 provides a statistic (40% of landfill waste) that supports banning plastic bottles. Source 1 actually argues FOR plastic bottles, which goes against the writer's position.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pick the dino on YOUR side - a convenience roar helps the other herd, not yours!

questions.question: Source 1: 'Later school start times would help teens because teenagers need more sleep to stay healthy.' Source 2: 'A neighboring district moved its start time to 8:30 a.m. and saw tardiness drop by 30% in one semester.' Which source is more useful for someone writing about whether start-time changes WORK IN PRACTICE?
questions.correctAnswer: Source 2, because it describes actual results from a real change
distractors: Source 1, because health is more important
Source 1, because it mentions teenagers directly
Both sources equally, because both mention start times
questions.explanation: Source 2 gives real-world results (30% drop in tardiness) from an actual policy change, which directly answers whether the change works in practice. Source 1 gives a general health reason but no evidence of results.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: practice needs proof - a real-world fossil beats a theory about dinosaur sleep!

questions.question: Source 1: 'A class survey found that 8 out of 10 students feel homework takes too long each night.' Source 2: 'Teachers assign homework so students can practice what they learned in class.' Which source would a student use to support the claim that homework should be reduced, and what kind of evidence is it?
questions.correctAnswer: Source 1; survey data showing most students struggle with homework load
distractors: Source 2; data from a classroom study
questions.explanation: Source 1 supports reducing homework with survey data (8 out of 10 students) showing the workload is a problem. Source 2 defends homework instead, so it cannot support the claim.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: survey the herd - when 8 of 10 dinos groan about homework, that's evidence, not just one dino's growl!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The scientist will analyze the test results,' what does 'analyze' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Analyze' means to examine something carefully in order to understand it. The context clue is that a scientist studies test results closely to find patterns.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: analyze is like a dino detective sniffing every clue - examine carefully!

questions.question: In the sentence 'Everyone in the group must contribute one idea,' what does 'contribute' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Contribute' means to give or add something, like time, ideas, or effort. The context clue is that each person adds one idea to the group.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: contribute is like each dino tossing a leaf onto the shared salad pile!

questions.question: In the sentence 'Desert temperatures vary a lot between day and night,' what does 'vary' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Vary' means to change or be different across a range. The context clue is that desert temperatures are very different during the day versus the night.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: vary is like Arizona weather - one minute hot sun, the next minute chilly night!

questions.question: In the sentence 'From the muddy footprints, we can infer that someone walked here,' what does 'infer' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Infer' means to figure something out using clues or evidence rather than being told directly. The context clue is that the muddy footprints are evidence used to conclude someone walked there.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: infer is like reading dino footprints - you figure out what happened from the clues!

questions.question: In the sentence 'Contrast the hot desert noon with the cold desert night,' what does 'contrast' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Contrast' means to point out how two things differ. The context clue is that the sentence pairs a hot noon with a cold night to highlight their differences.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: contrast is like a dino vs a lizard side by side - spot the differences!

questions.question: In the sentence 'Her speech made a significant difference in the vote,' what does 'significant' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Significant' means important or large enough to matter. The context clue is that her speech actually changed the vote, so its effect mattered.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: significant is like a T-Rex stomp - it really shakes things up!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The student will demonstrate how the volcano model erupts,' what does 'demonstrate' mean?
distractors: To describe it in a poem
questions.explanation: 'Demonstrate' means to show or prove how something works, often by doing it. The context clue is that the student shows the class how the volcano model erupts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: demonstrate is show-and-tell with a mini volcano - show it to know it!

questions.question: In the sentence 'Scholars interpret the ancient cave paintings in different ways,' what does 'interpret' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Interpret' means to explain or decide what something means, especially when it is not obvious. The context clue is that different scholars give different meanings to the same cave paintings.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: interpret is like translating cave drawings into a bedtime story - what does it mean?

questions.question: In the sentence 'The author emphasizes kindness by making it the theme of every chapter,' what does 'emphasize' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Emphasize' means to give something special importance or stress. The context clue is that the author repeats kindness as the theme of every chapter, stressing its importance.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: emphasize is like a dino roar for the most important part - make it LOUD!

questions.question: In the sentence 'One cup of water is not sufficient for the whole soccer team,' what does 'sufficient' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Sufficient' means enough to meet what is needed. The context clue is that one cup is not enough water for an entire soccer team.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sufficient is having enough leaf snacks for the whole dino herd - no empty bellies!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The mayor was reluctant to approve the new park because it cost too much money,' what does 'reluctant' mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Unwilling or hesitant to do something
distractors: Eager and excited to do something
questions.explanation: 'Reluctant' means unwilling or hesitant. The clue is that the mayor would not approve the park because of the cost.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: reluctant is when a dino drags its feet before stepping into the tar pit!

questions.question: Read this sentence: 'The detective gave a precise description of the suspect - six feet tall, wearing a red jacket, with a scar on his left cheek.' What does 'precise' mean here?
questions.explanation: 'Precise' means exact and detailed. The sentence proves it: the detective included height, clothing, and a scar, which are exact details.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: precise is like measuring your dino teeth one by one - exact!

questions.question: In the sentence 'The essay was so ambiguous that no two students agreed on what the author meant,' what does 'ambiguous' mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Open to more than one interpretation
questions.explanation: 'Ambiguous' means open to more than one interpretation. The clue is that students disagreed about the meaning, so the meaning was not clear or fixed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ambiguous is like blurry dino tracks in the mud - you can read them two ways!

questions.question: In the sentence 'Her argument was coherent: each point built on the last and the conclusion followed logically,' what does 'coherent' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Coherent' means clear, logical, and well organized. The sentence explains that each point built on the last and the conclusion followed logically.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a coherent argument is like a dino skeleton - every bone connected in the right order!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'Desert tortoises face two very different problems. First, the loss of native plants reduces their food supply. Second, ravens and coyotes attack more tortoises near highways. As a result, biologists say the tortoise population could drop by half within twenty years.' What text structure does the author use?
questions.explanation: The author names causes (loss of plants, more predators) and then gives the effect (the population could drop by half). That is cause and effect. There is no proposed solution, and no two things are compared.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cause and effect is a domino line of dinos - one falls, the rest wobble!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'Bats and owls both hunt at night, but they locate prey in different ways. Bats send out sound waves and listen for the echo, while owls rely on their sharp hearing and eyesight. Although both are successful night hunters, their methods show how different senses can solve the same problem.' What text structure does the author use?
questions.explanation: The passage compares how bats and owls hunt, pointing out similarities (both hunt at night) and differences (sound waves vs. hearing and eyesight). That is compare and contrast.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: comparing bats and owls is like lining up two fossils side by side to spot the differences!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'Before dawn, the hiker crossed the dry riverbed. By midmorning, storm clouds gathered over the ridge. Then the rain came, turning the riverbed into a rushing stream, and the hiker scrambled to higher ground. By sunset, the water had drained away, leaving only wet sand behind.' What text structure does the author use?
questions.explanation: The passage follows events in time order: before dawn, midmorning, then the rain, and by sunset. The signal words 'before dawn,' 'by midmorning,' 'then,' and 'by sunset' show chronological order.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: time order is like following dino footprints step by step - morning tracks to evening tracks!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'T-Rexy the T-Rex woke up to find his alarm clock had eaten his breakfast. He roared so loudly that the clock spit out the pancakes and ran away on its little legs. From that day on, T-Rexy set two alarm clocks - and ate breakfast before either one could.' What is the author's main purpose?
distractors: To persuade readers to eat breakfast
questions.explanation: The passage tells a silly, made-up story about a dinosaur and an alarm clock that eats breakfast. Its purpose is to amuse the reader, so the author wants to entertain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: when my breakfast gets eaten by a clock, the author just wants you to giggle!

questions.question: Read this passage: 'Every student should join a school club. Clubs build new skills, create friendships, and teach teamwork. If you want a stronger school experience, sign up for a club this week.' What is the author's main purpose?
distractors: To entertain with a funny story
questions.explanation: The author argues that clubs are valuable and urges the reader to 'sign up for a club this week.' The author is trying to convince the reader to take action, which is persuasion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: persuade is when a dino stomps its foot and says 'join my herd!'

questions.question: Read this passage: 'I stared at the trail map and realized we had taken the wrong turn hours ago. My legs were tired, my water bottle was empty, and the sun was dropping fast. That was the moment I decided to start carrying a compass on every hike.' What point of view is this passage written in?
questions.explanation: The narrator uses 'I' and 'my' to tell about their own experience on the trail. Writing from the narrator's own viewpoint with 'I' is first person point of view.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: first person is when I, T-Rexy, tell my own story - stomps and all!
